about: The raw JSON-RPC between our agent's MCP client and the contract-repository server, over stdio. It was captured with MCP_WIRE_LOG during the requirement-1 run (week9/trace-bolt-on.txt; unfiltered capture of both servers in week9/wire.raw.jsonl). 'message' is each message exactly as sent. 'annotations' are written by hand, one per top-level field.
model_call: The model (Gemini, called by generator.run in lib/agent.ts) runs only in the host: three times in the 107 s between message 5 and message 6 (it chose search_clauses, repeated it, then chose this get_amendment_chain call) and once after message 7 (to write the answer). No message on this wire is a model call, and the contract-repository server never calls a model.

annotations.method: "initialize" is always the first message. Our client (inside the host) opens the session, and nothing else may be sent until it is answered.
annotations.params: What the client brings to the negotiation: a protocol version, its capabilities, and who it is.
annotations.params.protocolVersion: "2025-11-25" is the newest MCP revision the SDK we run (1.32.1) speaks. The server must answer with this version or one it supports.
annotations.params.capabilities: {} means our client offers servers nothing back: no sampling (a server asking the host to run the model for it), no roots, no elicitation. So this server cannot get our model to run even if it wanted to.
annotations.params.clientInfo: Our host's client name and version. It's informational only, not authentication, and the server cannot verify it.
annotations.jsonrpc: "2.0" on every message: MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON object per line on the server's stdin (client→server) and stdout (server→client).
annotations.id: 0 is a request id, and the response must echo it. Ids are per connection: clause-search's connection also started at 0.

result.instructions: Knowledge team contract repository. Read-only lookups of executed documents by id: the record itself, its effective date, and its amendment chain.

annotations.jsonrpc: "2.0" on every message: MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON object per line on the server's stdin (client→server) and stdout (server→client).
annotations.id: 0 echoes request 1, so this is its answer. It arrived 1.8 s later, mostly npx/tsx starting the server process.
annotations.result: This is a success. A failure would come back under "error" (code + message) instead of "result".
annotations.result.protocolVersion: The server accepts 2025-11-25, so both sides now speak that revision.
annotations.result.capabilities: {tools:{listChanged:true}}: this server offers tools only, with no resources and no prompts, and may notify us if its tool list changes. There is no model-related capability anywhere in it.
annotations.result.serverInfo: contract-repository 2.3.0, self-reported and unverified. A hostile server can claim any name; trust comes from our config file, not from this field.
annotations.result.instructions: Optional free text the server would like in the model's context. Our agent never forwards it to the model: it is third-party text, so it is a prompt-injection surface.

annotations.method: The client confirms the handshake is done. Only after this may ordinary requests flow.
annotations.jsonrpc: "2.0" on every message: MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON object per line on the server's stdin (client→server) and stdout (server→client).
annotations.id (absent): There is no id because this is a notification: no response is expected, and none is sent.

annotations.method: "tools/list" is discovery. It replaces the hard-coded tool list: the agent learns these three tools exist only from the answer.
annotations.jsonrpc: "2.0" on every message: MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON object per line on the server's stdin (client→server) and stdout (server→client).
annotations.id: 1 is the next request id on this connection.
annotations.params (absent): No cursor, so this asks for the first page. lib/mcp-client.ts keeps asking while the result carries a nextCursor.

tools.name: get_contract
tools.title: Get contract by id
tools.description: Looks up one executed document by its id and returns its record: title, kind, effective date, the amendments recorded against it, and its full text as executed. The text is the original — amendments are listed but NOT applied; use get_amendment_chain for what changed.

contract_id.description: Document id as printed in its header, e.g. SA-2026-001.

tools.name: get_effective_date
tools.title: Get effective date
tools.description: Returns the date a document took effect, quoting the clause that says so, plus the dates its amendments took effect. When a document states no calendar date, says so and quotes its term clause instead.

contract_id.description: Document id, e.g. AMD-2026-001 or SA-2026-001.

tools.name: get_amendment_chain
tools.title: Get amendment chain
tools.description: Returns every amendment recorded against a contract, oldest first, with each one's effective date, the sections it replaces, and its text. Pass as_of (YYYY-MM-DD) to see which amendments were in force on that date.

contract_id.description: Id of the original contract, not of an amendment.

as_of.description: Date to evaluate the chain on, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

annotations.jsonrpc: "2.0" on every message: MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON object per line on the server's stdin (client→server) and stdout (server→client).
annotations.result.tools: Three tool definitions. Each has: name (what the model writes in its action); title (for humans); description (the only thing the model knows about when to use the tool, so the docstring is a prompt); inputSchema (JSON Schema generated from the server's zod, which our host renders into the system prompt); annotations.readOnlyHint (a claim the server makes about itself that nobody enforces); execution.taskSupport (SDK 1.32 field: not runnable as a long-running task).
annotations.result.nextCursor (absent): No cursor, so this is the whole list. These 3 tools plus the 4 from clause-search are the 7 the agent was given.

annotations.method: "tools/call" runs one tool. The client sends it only because the model, in its step-3 reply, chose this action; the client just forwards it. The 107 s gap since message 5 is the host calling the model three times.
annotations.params: Which tool to run, and with what.
annotations.params.name: get_amendment_chain is the model's choice, verbatim.
annotations.params.arguments: The model's arguments, verbatim. It took as_of=2026-10-15 from the question. The server validates them against the inputSchema it published in message 5.
annotations.jsonrpc: "2.0" on every message: MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON object per line on the server's stdin (client→server) and stdout (server→client).

content.text:
Amendment chain for SA-2026-001 (effective 2026-08-01), oldest first, evaluated on 2026-10-15:

1. AMD-2026-001 — effective 2026-10-01 — replaces §5 TERMINATION — IN FORCE on 2026-10-15
[AMD-2026-001 §1] 1. PURPOSE

This amendment modifies specific provisions of the
Service Agreement SA-2026-001.
[AMD-2026-001 §2] 2. TERMINATION NOTICE

Section 5 of the original Service Agreement is hereby
amended.

The original termination notice period of 30 days is
replaced with a termination notice period of 60 days.

The updated requirement is therefore:

Either party must provide 60 days written notice
before terminating the agreement.
[AMD-2026-001 §3] 3. EFFECTIVE DATE OF AMENDMENT

This amendment becomes effective on October 1, 2026.
[AMD-2026-001 §4] 4. OTHER TERMS

All other provisions of the original Service Agreement
remain unchanged and continue to remain in effect.
[AMD-2026-001 §5] 5. PRIORITY

If there is a conflict between this amendment and the
original Service Agreement regarding the termination
notice period, this amendment shall take precedence.

annotations.jsonrpc: "2.0" on every message: MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON object per line on the server's stdin (client→server) and stdout (server→client).
annotations.id: 2 echoes request 6. The answer took 82 ms on the wire; the server's own log says 3 ms of work.
annotations.result.content: A list of content blocks, here one text block. The host joins the text blocks and hands them to the model as the step-3 observation.
annotations.result.isError (absent): Absent means success. A tool failure (unknown id, a date before the contract took effect) also arrives here, as isError:true plus text: a normal result the model can read and recover from. A JSON-RPC "error" object is kept for protocol failures such as an unknown tool or invalid params.
annotations.result.structuredContent (absent): This server returns plain text only, with no machine-readable copy. Our agent reads [ID §N] clause labels out of the text, so citations from this server can be checked too.
